lines.en: “The Fourth Wall said. Wh ere am I.”
「Don't imi tate me.」

I was walking across the Story Horizon. More precisely, I had been doing nothing but walking for four days now. After wandering through endless mountains of garbage, anyone would feel like talking to a wall.
I muttered at a Story fragment lying on the ground.
“Kim Dokja thought. I should pick that up.”
There was still quite a bit of room left in the Infinite Dimension Space Coat, so I stuffed all the Stories I picked up into its remaining space. Then [Fourth Wall] answered.
「Id i ot.」
If there was any comfort to be had, it was that at least I wasn't talking to myself.
I had no idea what exactly [Fourth Wall] was, but at least it clearly wasn't hostile toward me. In fact, it was even protecting me from the [Exile Penalty]······.
「Sle, e, py.」
“Hang on a little longer. It's easier to move when you say something, anything.”
The [Exile Penalty] was hard to endure even now that I had an incarnation body, and there was still no end to the mountains of garbage.
This pain would probably continue until I returned to the scenarios.
[Some of the absorbed Stories are experiencing structural conflicts.]

Even though I was using [Lamarck’s Giraffe], an evolutionary attribute with relatively few side effects, the balance of Stories in my incarnation body was faltering. It wasn't serious yet, but if I fought or did anything unnecessary, my incarnation body could collapse again.
······Seriously, nothing ever came easy.
At this rate, I wondered when I'd ever get my revenge on the nebulas, but I couldn't rush things.
[You are approaching a scenario region.]
The first thing I had to do was acquire a scenario in the [Demon Realm].
Those Wenny men bastards had dumped me here without a care, but I knew exactly how to get a scenario in this place.
I already had a rough plan.
The route I was taking now was the same as Yoo Joonghyuk's in his 111th round.
So, unless some unusual variable came up along the way, nothing would derail my plan.
······Come to think of it, a lot had happened in Yoo Joonghyuk's 111th round.
I thought that was around the time the author of ‘Ways of Survival’ briefly fell into a slump.

It had been a little past chapter one thousand, and I remembered posting all kinds of things in the comments that I called advice. I didn't know whether it was because of my comments or something else, but a new character had suddenly appeared then, and the story's viewpoint had changed······.
Brrrr.
The [Dokkaebi Egg] tucked against my chest suddenly wriggled. After letting the egg absorb a few Story fragments, I stroked it.
“There, there, you little cutie.”
Thinking that the soul I'd saved would awaken as a new living creature left me feeling rather strange.
The egg would probably hatch within a month at the latest.
That would be when my plan really got underway.
Come to think of it, I couldn't keep calling this little one ‘Shin Yoosung’ after it hatched······. What should I name it?
「Just then, a sound reached Kim Dokja's ears.」
Rustle.

I crouched behind a mountain of garbage and held my breath. There weren't just one or two presences. There were at least dozens of them, as many as a hundred or so. After gauging the situation, I poked my head out slightly to take a look. Movements utterly devoid of vitality. Creatures resembling humans were rummaging through the heaps of Stories. Their identity was clear.
They were [Removal Slaves].

Those who gathered Story fragments near the Horizon for use as fuel, on the orders of the rulers who governed the Demon Realm. They had almost no capacity for reason (理智), so they wouldn't attack unless threatened first.
「Kim Dokja thought. If Removal Slaves are roaming around, an ‘industrial complex’ must be nearby.」
An [Industrial Complex] was something like a city here in the Demon Realm.
A place with a ‘factory’ that ground up broken Story fragments to generate energy, and a residential area surrounding that factory.
If I remembered correctly, the closest industrial complex to this spot was probably the [Syswitz Industrial Complex].
“Move it, move it! We're behind on today's fuel quota!”
Startled, I ducked behind the mountain of garbage again.
A demon with small wings and a single horn was fluttering around the area.
It was the industrial complex's overseer.
The fact that he had come along meant this ‘collection’ was on a fairly large scale.
Just then, a [Removal Slave] approached the back of the garbage mountain where I was hiding, perhaps having lost its way. Before I could get out of sight, our eyes met.
The [Removal Slave] staring at me with dull eyes looked like a chimpanzee rather than a human. It most likely belonged to one of the races abducted to the Demon Realm after its planet was destroyed.
Beings who had lost their own scenarios and come to depend on another being to survive.
I could see the brand [6424] stamped on its arm.
[The effect of the attribute ‘Demon King Candidate’ activates.]
[Demon King Candidate].
It was an attribute I'd acquired while progressing through the ‘73rd Demon King’ scenario.
Then I began to understand the words that had been unintelligible before.
―I, want, to, stop.
What?
―Kill, me, please.
Eyes pleading to be set free at last, as though existence itself were painful. I gazed at those pitiful eyes for a moment, then let out a deep sigh.
「Kim Dokja thought. It seems there's only one way.」
A little later, I was standing with the other Removal Slaves at the entrance to the [Industrial Complex]. I'd hidden my items, including the space coat, deep in the pile of Stories I'd brought.
In other words, I was naked.
It couldn't be helped if I wanted to look as much like a ‘Removal Slave’ as possible.
As a precaution, I'd also woven the brand of the dead ‘6424’ onto my left arm using a Story.
“Next!”
My plan was simple.
Slip in among the many Removal Slaves and enter the industrial complex.
The plan took advantage of the fact that inspections of slaves weren't as strict as those of other travelers.
“What's this? Today's haul is pathetic.”
But damn it, the overseer was fussier than I'd expected.
Thwack!
I swallowed as I watched the head of the ‘Removal Slave’ right in front of me burst apart.
“Hey, you there. Take this bastard along too. Shove him in the fuel tank.”
The overseer snickered as he tossed the Removal Slave toward a bucket as if it were a machine part.
[Demon Baron Chechefen].
He was no stronger than the lesser nobles I'd met in the [Dark Castle].
He might have a greater variety of Stories than those bastards in the [Dark Castle], but a baron was still a baron.
It wasn't as though I couldn't kill him if I put my mind to it and attacked.
The problem was what would happen after I killed him.

The owners of the [Industrial Complexes] were the Demon Realm's highest-ranking ‘dukes,’ and if I personally disposed of an industrial complex's overseer, there was a good chance its ‘duke’ would notice.
And needless to say, facing the Demon Realm's highest-ranking nobles with my incarnation body in its current incomplete state would be dangerous.
If necessary, I could use the [Demon King Candidate] attribute, but I didn't want to attract attention right from the start for no reason.
Anyway, for all those reasons, I couldn't help feeling nervous as I held out my basket of collected scraps.
If things went wrong here, my plans would become considerably harder to carry out.
“Oh, what's this! You've brought quite a lot!”

Fortunately, the overseer's face lit up at the heap of Story fragments I'd brought. I'd worried he might search through the pile and find my hidden items, but he didn't seem that thorough. Flapping his wings furiously like a tsetse fly, the overseer slapped my back and shouted.
“All of you, learn from this one! Huh? You all know how pathetic the hauls have been lately, don't you? At this rate, you'll be the next batch of fuel!”
Fear flashed in the Removal Slaves' eyes at the overseer's threat.
However much of their reason they had lost, the fear of a threat to their lives remained.
“Well done, 6424! Go on in!”
[You have entered a scenario region.]
Keeping out of the overseer's sight, I slipped away from the group of slaves at a suitable spot along the way.
I rummaged through the collected scraps and put on my items one by one, then kept what I needed and discarded the rest.
I made my way onto a main street, and before long, a wide-open square appeared.
Humans milling about. There were elves and demi-humans, and occasionally some who appeared to belong to demon species.
The Wenny man had been right when he said the Demon Realm was also a place where people lived.
A town where humans from different dimensions lived, along with all sorts of races forming communities together.
There were peddlers selling goods, and I could see people haggling over them.
It was the first town I'd visited in a while, since [Paradise].
A place where people lived and stories gathered.
A description from ‘Ways of Survival’ suddenly came to mind.
「An urban district enclosed by enormous ramparts.
Low slate roofs forming an uneven skyline.
Occasionally, vehicles equipped with steam engines could be seen passing along the main street.
A cityscape that seemed to mix civilizations at various stages of development.
Though it was a stage most constellations paid little attention to, this too was a place people called home.
A place where people gathered, each living with a scenario of their own.
This was the [Industrial Complex].」
Indeed, the scene was exactly as described.
Someone seeing an [Industrial Complex] in the Demon Realm for the first time might say this.
How could a place called the ‘Demon Realm’ look so peaceful?
Wasn't this far too similar to Earth, where ‘humans’ had lived together?
To people like that, I'd really like to recite a sentence from ‘Ways of Survival.’
「Looked at the other way around, perhaps that meant the human world had been just as terrible.」
Yes, that sentence.
For the first time in a while, recalling the contents of ‘Ways of Survival’ left me deeply moved.
The [Syswitz Industrial Complex] in the 73rd Demon Realm.
Here, I had to meet the people who would stand against the nebulas with me.
Of course, they themselves wouldn't have the slightest idea they would be doing any such thing······.
[Some of the absorbed Stories are experiencing structural conflicts.]
······I might have to move faster than I'd expected.
To make matters worse, even [Fourth Wall], which had been doggedly holding on, made a dispiriting remark.
「Slee, py.」
Huh? Hey, wait a second?
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ temporarily enters a state of silence.]
Damn it, of all places, here?
A chill rapidly seeped through my whole body, and sparks began to fly from various parts of my incarnation body.
Tzzzzzt.
As the [Exile Penalty] destabilized my incarnation body's presence, some of the people nearby noticed me.
“An e-exile!”
People hurriedly backing away from me as though they'd seen a source of infection.
I moved quickly, leaving the main street.
There wasn't much time left now.
『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.
Here, I had to find the story's ‘second protagonist.’
“Aaaah! An exile!”
“What? How did they get in?”
Incarnations shouting at the sight of me.
I pushed through the crowd and slipped into the city's shadows.
Tzzzzzt.

Because of the [Exile Penalty], pieces of Stories were falling from various parts of my body like blood. My right arm and the area around my heart were relatively stable thanks to the new Story fragments I'd absorbed, but the other parts weren't.
The incarnations had probably realized I was an exile after seeing this.
“Where'd they go? Shouldn't we report it?”
“Well······ they'll die soon enough like that. Let's just go.”
It wasn't strange.
Because this probably wasn't their first time seeing an exile.
They feared exiles simply because they didn't know what an exile might do.
After I spent a little while leaning against a wall in the alley and keeping quiet, the people looking around for me soon dispersed.
Vroooom―!
A procession of magic locomotives that appeared just then also helped smooth things over.
The incarnations recoiled in alarm at the sight of the magic locomotives coated in ominous black paint.
“Stand back! Nobles coming through!”
Magic locomotives racing toward the industrial complex's center.
I didn't know for sure, but they seemed to be visitors from another industrial complex.
High-ranking nobles of the Demon Realm were probably aboard. Those locomotives were carrying powerful beings at least on par with Reinheit, whom I'd met in [Paradise].
Roooar―!

I didn't know what was going on, but judging by their rush to the factory, they seemed to be carrying urgent news. The locomotives sped up without regard for the incarnations crossing the street. The commoners who had scrambled out of the way grumbled.
“That looks like a locomotive from [Gilobat]. Haven't we been seeing them often lately?”
“Who cares? It's the nobles' business.”
“We ought to care this time. There's talk that the 73rd Demon Realm is going to be unified.”
That was quite interesting, so I sharpened my hearing and focused on the talk circulating around me.
“The Demon Realm is going to be unified? Those dukes have finally gotten off their asses?”
“Yes, they say [Melledon] and [Bercan] have joined forces. Wouldn't that have [Syswitz] shitting himself?”
At the mention of the dukes who ruled the 73rd Demon Realm, other incarnations joined the conversation one by one.
“Hah! So that rumor was true? But······ our Demon Realm hasn't had a Demon King for thousands of years, has it?”
“So you're saying this ‘Demon King’ will come from our Demon Realm?”
Flustered by the barrage of questions, the incarnation who had first brought up the Demon King answered.
“I don't know for sure either. Rumor has it an oracle is circulating among the Demon Kings. About the appearance of a new Demon King······.”
“Each of those dukes must think they'll be the one.”
I'd seen a similar conversation in the original ‘Ways of Survival.’
This was exactly when rumors of that sort would be going around.
I'd arrived at just the right time.
A ‘Demon King’······.
I watched the procession of magic locomotives recede into the distance and thought.
This [Industrial Complex] had a class system too.
The ‘nobles,’ the class of those who ruled the industrial complex in the Demon Realm.
The ‘citizens (工民),’ the class of incarnations brought in from various dimensions.
And the ‘Removal Slaves,’ citizens who had lost their Stories and fallen into degradation.
Those were the only three classes for now, but if a [Demon King] arrived, everything would change.
A Demon King.
The sovereign of a Demon Realm, an absolute ruler who owned an entire world.
No race in the Demon Realm had any way to defy a Demon King.
Because here in the Demon Realm, a Demon King's presence was no less powerful than that of a Narrative-grade constellation.
The dukes of the 73rd Demon Realm were probably keeping a very wary eye on the prospect of such a Demon King's appearance.
Because once a Demon King appeared, their power structure would collapse in an instant.
But a ‘Demon King’ had to be created.
Because that was why I'd come to the ‘Demon Realm.’
―The second piece of information. Find the ‘Etika Clock Store.’
At the timely arrival of the message, I raised my head and looked at the sky.
I could faintly sense the Wenny men's presence in the darkness.
Fortunately, those Wenny men weren't entirely unscrupulous.
Among dokkaebis, ‘a bastard who learned business ethics from a Wenny man’ was practically an idiom, but that was because dokkaebis hated Wenny men······.
―There, you will be able to obtain what you desire.
When I gave a slight nod, the Wenny man's presence disappeared again.
Etika Clock Store.
Apparently, the Wenny men also knew there was a way to acquire a scenario in the [Demon Realm] at that clock store.
In fact, the original ‘Ways of Survival’ also contained information about that clock store.
Even so, I'd asked the Wenny men for information to avoid attracting unnecessary attention. You could say I needed to show myself acting in accordance with probability.
Tzzzzzt······.
I looked down at my left arm, which was on the verge of breaking apart.
Even if I went to the clock store right now, I wouldn't be able to acquire a ‘scenario’ immediately.
But there would be a way to reduce the [Exile Penalty].
Because that was what the Etika Clock Store existed for in the first place.
I set off without delay.
Not here.
Not down that alley either.
With my coat tightly fastened so no one could see where my Stories were breaking apart, I kept running through the alleys of the [Industrial Complex].
But I couldn't seem to find anything resembling a clock store.
Perhaps that was only natural.
Because things like clocks no longer held much meaning in the [Demon Realm]. Such objects only mattered to beings who lived short lives, like humans.
It would've been easy to find if I could read ‘Ways of Survival.’
With my smartphone gone, I had no way to read the text file.
If I'd known this would happen, I would've asked Bihyung to pack a smartphone for me beforehand······.
In the end, I was wondering whether I should take the risk and stop someone to ask, ‘Where is the Etika Clock Store?’ when someone happened to bump my shoulder while passing by.
“What the hell? Can't you use your damn eyes?”
“Oh, I'm sorry······.”
“You think sorry fixes everything? Damn it, you made me spill all the parts! Fuck!”
About fifteen years old, perhaps? A beautiful boy holding an armful of what looked like machine parts was glaring at me with a strangely haughty look.
“Uh······ well, I am sorry, but.”
I was about to ask whether that kind of foul language was really necessary, but the boy spoke before I could.
“If you're sorry, hurry up and pick them up, asshole!”
Overwhelmed by the strange aggression pouring from those beautiful lips, I hurriedly gathered the fallen parts.
For a moment, it felt as if the old ‘Kim Dokja’ had abruptly resurfaced.
Perhaps I'd been too diligent about picking up the parts; the boy snickered.
“Fuck, I'll let you off just this once. Watch it next time.”

After collecting the parts, the boy gave me that distinctive glare and ran off again. But why? Seeing that face had left me feeling as if I'd been hit on the back of the head with a hammer. It wasn't just belated resentment at being cursed out by someone younger than me.
That kid was······.
Like any fantasy novel, ‘Ways of Survival’ featured plenty of pretty and handsome characters.
For those who stood out even among its pretty and handsome characters, ‘Ways of Survival’ used the expression ‘beautiful enough to slap Yoo Joonghyuk in the face.’
Kyrgios Rodgraim, whom I'd met in [Peace Land], had been one such case.
But this world had beings even more beautiful than that ‘Kyrgios.’
What expression did it use for them, you ask?
「That kid had a face beautiful enough to slap Yoo Joonghyuk in the face twice.」
And even in ‘Ways of Survival,’ only three beings merited a description like that.
“Found you.”
With a deafening crash, an entire shelf in the shop shattered.
Damn it, that makes three times already. Buying replacement shelves is a pain too.
Aileen, the owner of the ‘Etika’ clock store, cursed inwardly while responding to the situation with her customary calm smile.
“What do you think you're doing?”
“What do you think? After going through the same thing three times, isn't it about time you got the message?”
“No, that's what I want to say. What on earth do you want from a mere clock store owner?”
Aileen tensely faced the two demons standing before her.
[Demon Baron Melen]
[Demon Earl Silocke]
The two demons bearing those respective names were well-known nobles here in the [Syswitz Industrial Complex]. The demons grinned at each other, and one of them extended a long arm.
“Urgh!”
With no time to dodge, Aileen groaned as her chin was seized.
Demon Earl Silocke snickered as he scrutinized the scars scattered across Aileen's pale skin.

“You certainly aren't an ordinary clock store owner. But you aren't so exceptional that our duke should have to ask you three times. Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage (三顧草廬), no less. Do you think you're some ‘Dragon Lying Down’?”
“······I don't know whose modifier that is, but I made what you asked for last time, didn't I? I can't help you this time.”
Rrrrrumble.
At those words, the air inside the clock store began to freeze.
The demon nobles had raised their power.
Just as she began to tremble and her face turned deathly pale.
“What's going on, Aileen? Did you borrow from a loan shark or something?”
Someone was standing at the clock store's door.
Demon Earl Silocke frowned when he saw the beautiful boy at the door.
“The clock store's foulmouth. Do you want to be executed?”
“I'll handle that one.”
Demon Baron Melen grabbed the beautiful boy by the throat and lifted the youth effortlessly.
Held by the throat, the beautiful boy stared down at Melen.
“I think this every time we come, but this one's quite pretty.”
“I think this every time I see you, but you look really disgusting.”
Melen's left hand struck the boy in the stomach. Despite the sound like a drum bursting, the boy's eyes remained utterly defiant. Melen smiled as though he liked that look.
“With looks like these, this one's more than pretty enough to become the duke's concubine.”
“What's the hourly pay there? If it's better than here, I might consider······.”
Another thwack rang out.
Aileen's expression hardened more and more as she watched the blood trickling from the boy's lips.
“Taking that child hostage won't get you anywhere.”
The demon let go as if he'd merely been playing around.
“Heh heh, who said we'd go that far? We're gentlemen.”
The beautiful boy fell from the air and landed on their backside with a groan.
“So you're refusing the offer? Is that what I should tell the duke?”
“Yes. I'm sorry, but······.”

They seemed surprisingly willing to leave without a fuss, and Aileen breathed an inward sigh of relief. It was understandable; this was one job she absolutely didn't want to take. If she accepted it, there was no telling how many more citizens would be sacrificed.
Silocke nodded as though he understood.
“Then we'll collect all the taxes you owe. The duke ordered us to bring them back.”
“Taxes? But I've had a tax exemption until now······.”
“Until now, yes. But not anymore.”
Of course. They wouldn't leave that easily.
Biting her lip, Aileen asked.
“······How much?”
50,000 coins.
Aileen was appalled by the enormous sum.
Things might be different in other scenario regions, but here in the [Syswitz Industrial Complex], coins were one of the highly valuable currencies.
“There are hardly any constellations here! There's no way I'd have that kind of money······.”
“If you won't pay, we'll take this brat with us. Putting this one among the concubines should fetch about 50,000 coins.”
Even at that casually delivered threat, the beautiful boy whistled.
“Wow! 50,000 coins! Aileen, if you get it, let's skip the taxes and run.”
“······I'll have screams coming out of that insolent mouth soon enough.”
“Really? Fuck, I can't wait.”

Despite the beautiful boy's bravado, despair flickered across Aileen's face. The two had been master and disciple for a long time, and she knew very well that the child's outwardly flippant words didn't reflect how the child felt inside. The demon earl delivered his final ultimatum.
“Aileen Makerfield. Accept the duke's offer. And bear in mind that this is the last time it will be offered.”
Aileen was the citizens' chairperson (議長). If they were taking such a hard line even with her, they had come with their minds firmly made up. After hesitating, Aileen opened her mouth.
Ding.
And someone entered the clock store.
“What?”
The first to greet me wasn't the clock store's owner.
Demon nobles visibly displeased by an unwelcome visitor.
I'd overheard enough of the conversation from outside to know what was happening.
The beautiful boy sprawled on the floor, eyes burning with hatred.
I answered while studying that beautiful boy instead of the demons.
“I'm a customer······.”
Despite my polite answer, the demon nobles' expressions turned menacing.
“A [Citizen]? I don't know where the hell you crawled in from, but get lost. We're collecting taxes.”
“Taxes······ You mean that thing where you pay a lot if you earn a lot, and still pay a lot if you earn little?”
“What?”
I walked past the demon nobles and approached the owner.
“Hey! Wait!”

The flustered demon noble reached out to grab me, but his arm never touched me. Astonishment appeared on his face as I shrugged off his attempt with an effortless movement. Rather than deal with them, I bent down to look at the clocks from the shattered shelf. I carefully picked up one of those clocks.
“You've got a lot of good things here.”
At that moment, as though she'd sensed something, Aileen, the clock store owner, approached me.
“······There are always good things here. Good owners are just hard to come by.”
For some reason, I felt like laughing.
Even the way she spoke was exactly as it had been in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Aileen Makerfield, a magic engineer from the planet [Lindberg].
I met Aileen's tense gaze.
The hands of a clock were probably turning inside her now too.
As she weighed whether this mysterious customer who had suddenly appeared would be her lifeline, or a disastrous move that would send the situation spiraling into the abyss······.
I decided to ease her worries a little.
“I'd like to order something a little special. Can you make one for me?”
At my words, Aileen's eyes widened.
Because only one kind of customer came here to commission ‘something special.’
Watching the demon nobles' reactions, Aileen asked cautiously.
“······And the commission fee?”
I grinned, looked at her once, then at the nobles glaring at me, and spoke.
“Wait, you're the one from earlier······!”
The beautiful boy's eyes widened in recognition. But before the youth could say anything, the quick-witted Aileen swiftly accepted my coins.
“50,000 coins. All right.”
“Th-that's really 50,000 coins······?”
Aghast, the beautiful boy looked back and forth between Aileen and me, mouth hanging open.
Across the scenarios as a whole, 50,000 coins wasn't that large a sum, but by the standards of the [Demon Realm], it was considerable.
Because this was a region constellations rarely visited due to the influence of the Demon Kings.
Of course, by my standards, 50,000 coins was pocket change.
[The single-part ‘Kim Dogeza’s Legend’ has been completed on the planet ‘Peace Land.’]
[The region's pioneers preach faith in you.]
[You have acquired 15,000 coins.]
I even had a place sending me coins in real time, you see.
This was the nice thing about being a constellation.
Because even without receiving sponsorship, simply becoming famous made you money.
The demon nobles, who had frozen in bewilderment, finally reacted.
“Who are you?”
I examined their information.
One was [Demon Earl Silocke].
And the other was [Demon Baron Melen].
They were fairly well-known tax collectors in the [Syswitz Industrial Complex].
“I told you. A customer.”

Normally, I would've been polite and deferential, but good manners only backfired with bastards like these. Because they were like hyenas: even if you had nothing, you had to act as if you had plenty to frighten them.
“You bastard, now······!”
At my tone, Demon Baron Melen raised his aura.
“Stop, Melen.”
Silocke, who had been watching from beside him, urged Melen to stop.
As expected, someone who'd made it to earl seemed to know how to read the room.
[The character ‘Demon Earl Silocke’ shows curiosity toward you.]
[Your understanding of the character ‘Demon Earl Silocke’ increases.]
I seized the opportunity and activated my skill.
[Activating the exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’!]
Then I began to hear Silocke's thoughts.
「He can easily pay 50,000 coins.」
「That's an amount an ordinary citizen could never afford. And he's so relaxed. He must consider 50,000 coins mere pocket change.」
「Who is he? I've never seen him in this district before. Wait, that demonic energy······.」
「Could it be······?」
Just as I'd expected. I knew he'd be thinking that.
I thought this might actually work out well.
The [Syswitz Industrial Complex] was already buzzing with talk of a new Demon King. In that case, it wouldn't hurt to let slip some information these guys could conveniently misunderstand.
I spoke with as much bravado as I could muster.
“You should already have some idea who I am.”
Silocke's complexion changed sharply at my Yoo Joonghyuk-like tone. As though his suspicions had been confirmed, he belatedly nodded and became respectful.
“My belated greetings, Your Demonship (貴魔). Might you be visiting from the [Gilobat Industrial Complex]?”
“At least your ears seem to work.”
“But we received no notification that you would be visiting this district······.”
“Must I inform even low-ranking underlings like you of my itinerary?”
“Well······ I apologize.”
My brief answer seemed to explain everything to him.
「The authority to travel without prior notification. That must mean he's at least a marquis.」
「Nothing good will come of getting entangled with the [Gilobat Industrial Complex].」
Having arrived at a splendid misunderstanding, Silocke bowed to me, then jerked his chin at Melen.
“Let's go.”
“Pardon? But······.”
“We only need to collect what's owed.”
At his superior's coolheaded judgment, Melen belatedly came to his senses and nodded too. After collecting 50,000 coins from Aileen, Melen spat out his words in a harsh voice.
“You got lucky this time. But don't think you will next time, Aileen.”
With those words, the two demon nobles left the clock store.
That Silocke fellow would probably report this to his superior immediately.
It didn't matter. It wasn't as though I hadn't thought that far ahead.
After the storm had passed, the clock store was filled with a sense of emptiness.
It was the beautiful boy who broke the mood.
“······You're pretty good, huh? Who the hell are you?”
I smiled quietly at the youth looking up at me with sparkling eyes.
“You're taking the commission, right?”
Finally coming to her senses, Aileen looked at me.
“Um······ but are you a noble?”
Well, if even the demons had misunderstood, there was no reason Aileen couldn't make the same mistake.
I shook my head and spoke.
“I don't belong to a demon species.”
Instead of answering, I quietly took off my coat.
Broken pieces of Stories trickled down amid sparks.
Seeing my body, Aileen approached with a shocked expression.

“Damn it! I can’t stop crying!”
[Your fame in the 73rd Demon Realm increases.]
[You have obtained 1,500 coins.]
Wait, was I really this popular?
I suddenly began to regret cosplaying as Yoo Joonghyuk.
But I couldn’t tell them now that it was actually me.
―Let’s meet again, Yoo Joonghyuk.
As the scenario finally reached its closing act, people began to wail.
Some were so overwhelmed with emotion that they couldn’t pull themselves out of it.
Jang Hayoung murmured with a rapt expression.
“Ah, I wonder if he already has a girlfriend.”
My heart lurched.
“What? Who?”
“The Demon King of Salvation. Do you happen to know him, too?”
“I do know him, but······.”
I frowned as I looked into Jang Hayoung’s beautiful eyes.
Plump, snow-white cheeks and clear eyes.
In sheer beauty, that face really was extraordinary. But······.
“Aren’t you a guy?”
If I remembered correctly, Jang Hayoung was male.
Because that damned author of ‘Ways of Survival’ had accepted every one of my comments, then changed exactly one thing however they pleased.
And that was this kid’s gender.
Jang Hayoung frowned and said.
“Trying to judge everything by appearances. Typical Earthling.”
Just as I was about to reply, the tavern owner suddenly turned off the lights.
Then he addressed the entire tavern in a very low voice.
“Night is coming.”

At those few quiet words, a deep silence spread through the tavern from the owner outward. A silence far more taut and sharp than when the word ‘Disaster’ had come up earlier. Meeting my eyes, Jang Hayoung put an index finger to their lips.
“Shh.”
Looking more closely, I saw it wasn’t just this tavern.
Other taverns and shops along the street were closing their doors and turning off their lights, too. Sounds were vanishing in an instant.
As though the entire [Industrial Complex] were sinking into the deep sea.
From the deserted street, something like the sound of an eerie flute began to drift in.
I saw several citizens cover their ears to shut out the sound.
At that moment, something came back to me, too.
「A special [Night] comes to the Demon Realm.」
Listening to the [Fourth Wall]’s voice, I recalled the setting of ‘Ways of Survival.’
「All citizens of the [Industrial Complex] fear the nobles. It wasn’t simply because the nobles were strong. It was because of this [Night], which came once every three days.」
“Please just pass us by. Please······.”
Someone murmured those words. How much time passed after that? With a crackling sound as the windows froze over, I sensed something passing along the street.
Sssssss.

Holding their breath, the citizens acted as though they couldn’t see it. Some even bowed their heads all the way down against the tables. The shadow of an enormous scythe, glimpsed now and then beyond the frozen windows.
「When Night falls, an [Executioner] appears in the Industrial Complex.」
「If the citizens have a [Revolutionary], the nobles have an [Executioner].」
The root of the citizens’ inability to resist the nobles despite their terror, and the reason the duke could maintain his position of absolute power in this Industrial Complex.
It all came down to the existence of that [Executioner].
Creeeeak.
The moment the tavern door opened, everyone squeezed their eyes shut.
From the deep darkness came a voice like glass being scratched.
[Who is the Re vo lu tion ar y.]
A body that looked about twice the size of an adult man’s, with an appearance reminiscent of the Grim Reaper.
The black cape draped over it concealed its face, but the sinister aura it exuded was enough for me to sense its power.
[The target is currently under the protection of the scenario.]
[The target is currently invincible.]
No being could stand against that [Executioner] inside the [Industrial Complex] at Night.
The owner who had served me food and the people who had noisily chatted while watching the scenario were all staring at the floor, their faces deathly pale.
Tonight, the [Executioner] had chosen this tavern as its execution ground.
Someone here would certainly die in this very place tonight.
[Who is the Re vo lu tion ar y.]
People curled in on themselves whenever the Executioner’s scythe swept past them. It looked almost like a game. As I studied the creature closely, Jang Hayoung tugged at my collar in alarm.
“Don’t make eye contact.”
At that faint sound, the [Executioner] turned toward us.
More precisely, toward Jang Hayoung, who was swearing.
Watching the [Executioner] slowly approach, Jang Hayoung began to tremble.
The face of someone sensing their own impending death.
I planted a hand on the utterly terrified Jang Hayoung’s head and slowly rose from my seat.
Leaving Jang Hayoung gaping in shock, I raised my head. The [Executioner] was watching me with ominous eyes.
「Kim Dokja thought. What would Yoo Joonghyuk have done?」
He would never have revealed himself here.
Yoo Joonghyuk would have kept himself hidden to the very end, looking for the situation that would benefit him most.
He would have completed every kind of investigation to enter the [Industrial Complex]’s scenario, and wrestled alone with the question of who the [Revolutionary] was.
「Kim Dokja thought. That was why the bastard had regressed hundreds of times.」
The [Executioner] smoothly tightened its grip on the scythe and addressed me in a spine-chilling voice.
[Who are y ou.]
At that moment, with everyone in the tavern watching me, I spoke in a voice they could all hear clearly.
“I am the ‘Revolutionary.’”
